name: Leprino Foods Company
old_description: We started in 1950 as a small family-run grocery store in Denver, Colorado. Today, Leprino is proud to be the world’s largest producer of mozzarella cheese and a leading manufacturer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein and other high-quality dairy ingredients.
about:
Leprino Foods Company began in 1950 when Mike Leprino Sr. started making mozzarella cheese in the back room of his family's corner grocery store at 38th Avenue and Shoshone Street in Denver, Colorado. The business incorporated as Leprino Cheese Manufacturing Company in the 1960s and was renamed Leprino Foods Company in the 1970s to reflect its expanding portfolio. It remains family-owned today.

The company produces mozzarella and pizza cheese, whey protein, lactose, micellar casein, and other dairy ingredients. Its patented "Same Day Dice" process turns fresh milk into cheese in four hours, and its Quality-Locked Cheese uses individual quick freezing to preserve flavor. Operations span manufacturing facilities on three continents, including a 640,000-square-foot plant in Lemoore, California, with over 1,100 employees, and a new $1 billion facility in Lubbock, Texas. Global headcount exceeds 5,000.

Leprino supplies food and nutrition brands worldwide, including major pizza chains, with products sold in more than 70 countries. A strategic alliance with Dairy Farmers of America secures milk supply, and joint ventures in Europe, Latin America, and Asia extend its reach.

The company emphasizes its "Leprino Difference" — quality, service, competitive price, and ethics — and a Global Responsibility framework covering product, supply chain, environment, people, and communities.

about:
Levine Contract Furniture Group was founded in 1973 by Harvey Levine at a desk in the Pan Am Building on 42nd Street in New York City. The family-owned business began with sales conducted in person or by phone, and orders sent by mail. John Calvano joined the company in 1975, expanding its sales territory across the region.

The firm markets contract furniture for corporate, healthcare, education, and retail environments, representing manufacturing partners such as Egan. It maintains an in-stock inventory that ships in as little as 48 hours, fulfilling orders ranging from a few desks to 50,000-square-foot office installations. Custom solutions include bespoke furniture, architectural elements, power and data integration, and privacy pods, all tailored to client specifications.

Levine serves corporate workplaces, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, and retail spaces. Its healthcare portfolio addresses clinical, public, and professional furnishings for wellness interiors, while its education line focuses on technology management and durability for collaborative learning zones. Corporate clients receive agile furniture systems for open-plan, private office, conference, and huddle-room settings.

The company emphasizes fast turnaround on stocked items, deep vertical expertise in healthcare and education, and a single-source approach for custom projects that integrate technology and material selection. Its showroom in New York City offers virtual and in-person tours, continuing education courses, and COM/COL management for specifiers.

name: Liberate Medical
old_description: VentFree contracts the expiratory muscles during mechanical ventilation to keep them active.
about:
Liberate Medical is based in Crestwood, Kentucky. The company develops the VentFree Respiratory Muscle Stimulator, a medical device designed to address respiratory muscle atrophy in mechanically ventilated patients.

The VentFree system uses proprietary non-invasive neuromuscular electrical stimulation to contract the abdominal wall muscles in synchrony with exhalation during mechanical ventilation. Therapy can begin from day one of ventilation while patients are sedated or delirious, and the device is described as quick and simple to use. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

The company serves the critical care and respiratory care segments of the healthcare industry. Its customers include hospitals and ICU teams managing mechanically ventilated patients, particularly those requiring more than four days of ventilation who face high rates of weaning failure and post-discharge complications.

Liberate Medical states that its approach may reduce abdominal muscle atrophy and shorten the duration of mechanical ventilation. A pilot randomized controlled trial found that ventilation duration and ICU length of stay were shorter in patients receiving VentFree stimulation compared to placebo, potentially reducing morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs.

name: Lincoln Electric Products Co.
old_description: We build a full range of highly customizable electrical distribution equipment.
about:
Lincoln Electric Products Co. has operated from Union, New Jersey since its founding in 1949. The company began as a manufacturer of electrical distribution equipment serving the tri-state region, built on the core values established by founder Irving Leff. Today it remains a family-owned and operated business, led by President Matthew Leff, with ownership and management continuing along the same lines set at inception.

The company produces a full range of highly customizable electrical distribution equipment, including switchboards and integrated electrical systems. All equipment is manufactured in the United States under an ISO 9001:2015 certified quality management system. The firm emphasizes a design and integration process supported by experienced project managers and engineers, targeting lead times as short as four weeks while maintaining cost efficiency. An two-year warranty covers all equipment.

Customers span the tri-state area and include businesses and institutions that require reliable power infrastructure with minimal downtime. The company describes its solutions as the backbone of reliable power for operations that cannot afford interruption, serving industries, businesses, and communities with tailored electrical distribution products.

The company states its differentiation rests on precision craftsmanship, dependable performance, and customer-focused service — values traced to its founding. Ongoing investment in advanced technologies and efficient manufacturing processes is cited as the means to stay ahead of industry demands, with a mission to develop collaborative, trusting relationships and produce reliable, well-engineered, high-quality electrical equipment.

name: Lincoln Industries Manufacturing of WI, LLC
old_description: Lincoln Industries is the largest and most diverse privately-held metal finishing company in North America. We develop technical solutions that move our customers forward by bringing their visions to life.
about:
Lincoln Industries operates from Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, where it has built a privately held metal finishing business spanning more than seven decades. The company describes itself as the largest and most diverse privately held metal finisher in North America, though it does not disclose a founding year or founder names in its public materials.

The core operation centers on precision electroplating and expanded in-house coating capabilities, serving as a metal finishing partner for original equipment manufacturers. In recent years the company has broadened its truck-component portfolio beyond exhaust systems to include bumpers, internal cab parts, grab bars, engine components, emblems, and heat-management solutions, leveraging automation to handle complexity. A 2025 launch added a Fourth Wall division that supplies LED display systems for sports venues, commercial installations, and outdoor environments.

Customers come from agriculture, automotive, appliances, motorsports, powersports, oil and gas, tools, and heavy-duty truck sectors. The truck segment is highlighted as a major growth area, with the company noting its ability to evolve alongside major heavy-duty truck OEMs.

Leadership frames the business around developing technical solutions that move customers forward, emphasizing continuous improvement — 391 projects reported — and a culture of wellness and community engagement. The expansion into coating and LED displays is presented as a response to customer demand for integrated, value-added manufacturing.

name: Lincoln Plastics
old_description: Lincoln Plastics is a Nebraska-based custom extrusion manufacturer.
about:
Lincoln Plastics, headquartered in Lincoln, Nebraska, began operations in 1948 as a custom plastic profile extrusion company. Today it operates as part of the PCE family of companies alongside its sister division, HTI Plastics, which provides injection molding services.

The company specializes in custom plastic profile extrusion, including co-extrusion of two materials or colors, flexible and rigid profiles, pipe and tube, and proprietary cord-management products sold under the Flexiduct brand. Its 25,000-square-foot facility is ISO 9001:2015 certified and runs in-line quality checks throughout production.

Lincoln Plastics serves original equipment manufacturers in the center-pivot irrigation market, supplying drop pipes, hose weights, drive-shaft tubes, and PVC U-pipe and U-joint covers. It also provides cord and cable management solutions for office, garage, tradeshow, and residential customers, and works with industrial OEMs nationwide and internationally.

The company emphasizes quick order turnaround, a Midwest location for fast delivery, and a commitment to customer service that includes design assistance and quality plans tailored to each part.

name: Little Homestead Furniture
old_description: Solid American Hardwood Furniture, Sofas and Seating since 1987
about:
Little Homestead Furniture was founded in 1987 by a local architect in Rockville, Maryland. The independent retailer operates a showroom in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, specializing in solid American hardwood furniture sourced from domestic manufacturers.

The store carries bedroom, dining, living room, home office, TV/media, and youth bedroom collections. Its inventory is produced by a network of small family-owned factories in New England—particularly Vermont—and additional manufacturing partners in Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Texas, North Carolina, and Virginia. All pieces are built from solid hardwoods such as cherry, maple, oak, and walnut, and the company offers a made-to-order program that allows dimensional changes, stain adjustments, and feature modifications often at little or no extra cost.

Little Homestead primarily serves residential customers in the D.C. region who favor classic, timeless designs—Shaker, Mission, Arts & Crafts, and contemporary motifs—and who prioritize well-made, domestically produced furniture over mass-market alternatives.

The business positions itself as an antidote to the ubiquitous “distressed” and “weathered” finishes common at large retailers, emphasizing responsibly harvested lumber, traditional joinery (dovetailed drawers, mortise-and-tenon construction), and durable, environmentally friendly finishes. The made-to-order flexibility is cited as a key differentiator.

old_description: A Cut Above the Rest: Your Trusted Steel & Aluminum Distributor
about:
Loftis Steel & Aluminum, Inc. is a family-owned metals distributor and processor based in Nashville, Tennessee. The company was founded in 2000 as a family business and has since formed a dynamic partnership with Tennessee Die Supply, operating from a Nashville facility that serves the Southeast region. The company describes its legacy as one of resilience, growth, and deep industry roots.

The company supplies a range of metals including aluminum, tool steels, and other alloys, and provides advanced processing services such as precision laser cutting, waterjet cutting, and CAD design support. Its in-house team includes four CAD engineers who assist with design work, print clean-up, and expert guidance. Loftis also operates its own delivery fleet alongside shipping partners to serve customers across the region.

Loftis serves a broad set of industries including aerospace, automotive, construction, energy, firearms, government, machine shops, general manufacturing, medical, and oil & gas. Its customers range from local machine shops and auto parts manufacturers to government agencies, with the company positioning itself as a specialist in each sector.

The company emphasizes its employee-centric culture and generational experience as differentiators, and states it can deliver products and services up to fifty percent faster than competitors without sacrificing attention to detail.

name: Logix, LLC
old_description: is to partner with our customers on their electrification journey towards a more sustainable future.
about:
Logix, LLC was founded in 2015 in Belfast, Maine, by Josh and Rachele as a family‑owned solar and heat‑pump installation business originally named SolarLogix. The company rebranded to Logix as its service lines expanded beyond solar to cover a broader range of electrification technologies.

Today Logix provides turnkey installation of solar photovoltaic systems, air‑source and ground‑source heat pumps, heat‑pump water heaters, electric‑vehicle charging stations, battery backup systems, and electrical service upgrades. A crew of roughly 35 technicians serves residential and commercial customers across central and eastern Maine, handling everything from initial design and incentive paperwork to ongoing maintenance.

The client base spans homeowners looking to cut utility bills and businesses seeking to decarbonize operations. Projects referenced in testimonials include residential heat‑pump and water‑heater retrofits, commercial solar arrays, and battery backup installations for both sectors.

The company emphasizes its fluency with Efficiency Maine rebates, federal tax credits, and USDA REAP grants, which it says can save customers thousands of dollars. Logix also highlights its certified technicians, a satisfaction guarantee, and a family‑run culture that prioritizes safety and long‑term customer relationships.

Logo Magic has been locally owned and operated in Dickinson, North Dakota, since 1989. The company began as a custom apparel and promotional products provider, focusing on screen printing and embroidery for businesses, schools, and groups in the region.

The shop offers in-house screen printing, embroidery, and laser etching, along with graphic design and custom art services. It sources blank apparel from vendors such as Sanmar, S&S Activewear, and Richardson Caps, then decorates items ranging from flame‑resistant workwear and corporate polos to team uniforms and promotional goods like bags, drinkware, and magnets. The company also builds and administers custom e‑commerce stores for corporate programs, fundraisers, and group orders.

Customers include small and large businesses, industrial firms needing FR gear, schools, athletic teams, clubs, and individuals ordering for reunions or fundraisers. The company serves a broad range of sectors but emphasizes corporate branding, industrial safety apparel, education, and sports organizations.

Logo Magic differentiates itself with free custom art on most apparel orders, no‑minimum laser etching, quick turnaround times on embroidery and screen printing, and a hands‑on approach that guides clients from design through production to pickup or delivery.
